        "originalContents": "\n\nexport const useBlockEditor = ({\n  aiToken,\n  ydoc,\n  provider,\n}: {\n  aiToken: string\n  ydoc: YDoc\n  provider?: TiptapCollabProvider | null | undefined\n}) =\u003e {\n  const leftSidebar = useSidebar()\n  const [collabState, setCollabState] = useState\u003cWebSocketStatus\u003e(\n    provider ? WebSocketStatus.Connecting : WebSocketStatus.Disconnected\n  )\n  const { setIsAiLoading, setAiError } = useContext(EditorContext)\n\n  const editor = useEditor(\n    {\n      immediatelyRender: false,\n      autofocus: true,\n      onCreate: ({ editor }) =\u003e {\n        if (provider) {\n          provider.on('synced', () =\u003e {\n            if (editor.isEmpty) {\n              editor.commands.setContent(initialContent)\n            }\n          })\n        } else {\n          editor.commands.setContent(initialContent)\n          editor.commands.focus('start', { scrollIntoView: true })\n        }\n      },\n      extensions: [\n        ...ExtensionKit({\n          provider,\n        }),\n        provider\n          ? Collaboration.configure({\n              document: ydoc,\n            })\n          : undefined,\n        provider\n          ? CollaborationCursor.configure({\n              provider,\n              user: {\n                name: randomElement(userNames),\n                color: randomElement(userColors),\n              },\n            })\n          : undefined,\n        Ai.configure({\n          appId: TIPTAP_AI_APP_ID,\n          token: aiToken,\n          baseUrl: TIPTAP_AI_BASE_URL,\n          autocompletion: true,\n          onLoading: () =\u003e {\n            setIsAiLoading(true)\n            setAiError(null)\n          },\n          onSuccess: () =\u003e {\n            setIsAiLoading(false)\n            setAiError(null)\n          },\n          onError: (error) =\u003e {\n            setIsAiLoading(false)\n            setAiError(error.message)\n          },\n        }),\n      ].filter((e) =\u003e !!e),",

      "codeBlock": {
        "contents": "import {MindMapBottomMenu} from '@/features/mindmap/components/menus/mindmap-bottom-menu/mindmap-bottom-menu'\nimport {useAssistantInstructions} from '@assistant-ui/react'\n\nexport function BottomMenuAiWrapped() {\n  useAssistantInstructions({\n    instruction: &#96;\n     # MindMapBottomMenu: Logic, Features, Behavior, and Data Flow\n\n## Overview\n\n\\&#96;MindMapBottomMenu\\&#96; is a highly interactive, stateful React component (Next.js 15, functional style) that serves as the primary AI/Oracle input and control bar for the Mind Map feature. It orchestrates user input, AI chat, database search, and dynamic mind map graph updates, integrating with multiple contexts, actions, and UI modules.\n\n---\n\n## Key Modules and Architecture\n\n- **Contexts**\n  - \\&#96;useMindMap\\&#96;: Provides all graph manipulation and data loading functions (nodes, edges, queries, etc.).\n  - \\&#96;useSessionNotes\\&#96;: Allows saving AI chat messages as session notes.\n\n- **Actions**\n  - \\&#96;initiateDatabaseTableQuery\\&#96;: Triggers a search/query against a database table.\n  - \\&#96;xataToXYFlow\\&#96;: Converts database/AI results into graph nodes/edges for visualization.\n  - \\&#96;askAIAction\\&#96;: Sends a question to the AI for a specific table/model.\n\n- **AI Integration**\n  - \\&#96;useAssistant\\&#96; (from \\&#96;@ai-sdk/react\\&#96;): Manages AI chat state, message history, input, and error handling.\n\n- **UI Components**\n  - \\&#96;OracleInput\\&#96;: Input field with command/model context.\n  - \\&#96;OracleCommandMenu\\&#96;: Command palette for selecting actions (chat, search, scrape, etc.).\n  - \\&#96;UltraterrestrialModelSelection\\&#96;: Model/entity type selector.\n  - \\&#96;MindMapMessages\\&#96;: Renders chat/AI messages.\n  - \\&#96;SessionNotes\\&#96;: Displays session notes.\n\n---\n\n## Features and Behaviors\n\n### 1. **Session and Message Persistence**\n- Generates or retrieves a unique session ID (UUID) per user/session, stored in \\&#96;localStorage\\&#96;.\n- Persists chat messages to \\&#96;localStorage\\&#96;",
        "detailedLines": [
          {

            "isSignature": true,

            "text": "export function BottomMenuAiWrapped() {"

          {
            "lineNumber": 5,
            "text": "  useAssistantInstructions({"
          },

            "lineNumber": 6,
            "text": "    instruction: &#96;"

          {
            "lineNumber": 7,
            "text": "     # MindMapBottomMenu: Logic, Features, Behavior, and Data Flow"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 8
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 9,
            "text": "## Overview"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 10
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 11,
            "text": "\\&#96;MindMapBottomMenu\\&#96; is a highly interactive, stateful React component (Next.js 15, functional style) that serves as the primary AI/Oracle input and control bar for the Mind Map feature. It orchestrates user input, AI chat, database search, and dynamic mind map graph updates, integrating with multiple contexts, actions, and UI modules."
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 12
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 13,
            "text": "---"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 14
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 15,
            "text": "## Key Modules and Architecture"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 16
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 17,
            "text": "- **Contexts**"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 18,
            "text": "  - \\&#96;useMindMap\\&#96;: Provides all graph manipulation and data loading functions (nodes, edges, queries, etc.)."
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 19,
            "text": "  - \\&#96;useSessionNotes\\&#96;: Allows saving AI chat messages as session notes."
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 20
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 21,
            "text": "- **Actions**"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 22,
            "text": "  - \\&#96;initiateDatabaseTableQuery\\&#96;: Triggers a search/query against a database table."
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 23,
            "text": "  - \\&#96;xataToXYFlow\\&#96;: Converts database/AI results into graph nodes/edges for visualization."
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 24,
            "text": "  - \\&#96;askAIAction\\&#96;: Sends a question to the AI for a specific table/model."
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 25
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 26,
            "text": "- **AI Integration**"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27,
            "text": "  - \\&#96;useAssistant\\&#96; (from \\&#96;@ai-sdk/react\\&#96;): Manages AI chat state, message history, input, and error handling."
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 28
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 29,
            "text": "- **UI Components**"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 30,
            "text": "  - \\&#96;OracleInput\\&#96;: Input field with command/model context."
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 31,
            "text": "  - \\&#96;OracleCommandMenu\\&#96;: Command palette for selecting actions (chat, search, scrape, etc.)."
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 32,
            "text": "  - \\&#96;UltraterrestrialModelSelection\\&#96;: Model/entity type selector."
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 33,
            "text": "  - \\&#96;MindMapMessages\\&#96;: Renders chat/AI messages."
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 34,
            "text": "  - \\&#96;SessionNotes\\&#96;: Displays session notes."
          },

            "lineNumber": 35
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 36,
            "text": "---"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 37
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 38,
            "text": "## Features and Behaviors"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 39
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 40,
            "text": "### 1. **Session and Message Persistence**"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 41,
            "text": "- Generates or retrieves a unique session ID (UUID) per user/session, stored in \\&#96;localStorage\\&#96;."
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 42,
            "text": "- Persists chat messages to \\&#96;localStorage\\&#96; for session continuity."
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 43
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 44,
            "text": "### 2. **AI Chat and Oracle Actions**"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 45,
            "text": "- Supports freeform chat, deep research, scraping, and analysis via AI."
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 46,
            "text": "- Handles chat input, message submission, and displays AI responses."
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 47,
            "text": "- Error handling: Catches and displays AI errors in the UI."
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 48
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 49,
            "text": "### 3. **Database Search and Mind Map Updates**"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 50,
            "text": "- Allows searching for entities (events, personnel, organizations, etc.) by type and keyword."
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 51,
            "text": "- Prevents duplicate searches and nodes in the graph."
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 52,
            "text": "- Adds user input nodes, result nodes, and edges to the mind map."
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 53,
            "text": "- Supports dynamic layout (horizontal, vertical, radial, grid) based on entity type."
          },

            "lineNumber": 54
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 55,
            "text": "### 4. **Command Palette and Model Selection**"

            "lineNumber": 56,

        "originalContents": "import {MindMapBottomMenu} from '@/features/mindmap/components/menus/mindmap-bottom-menu/mindmap-bottom-menu'\nimport {useAssistantInstructions} from '@assistant-ui/react'\n\nexport function BottomMenuAiWrapped() {\n  useAssistantInstructions({\n    instruction: &#96;\n     # MindMapBottomMenu: Logic, Features, Behavior, and Data Flow\n\n## Overview\n\n\\&#96;MindMapBottomMenu\\&#96; is a highly interactive, stateful React component (Next.js 15, functional style) that serves as the primary AI/Oracle input and control bar for the Mind Map feature. It orchestrates user input, AI chat, database search, and dynamic mind map graph updates, integrating with multiple contexts, actions, and UI modules.\n\n---\n\n## Key Modules and Architecture\n\n- **Contexts**\n  - \\&#96;useMindMap\\&#96;: Provides all graph manipulation and data loading functions (nodes, edges, queries, etc.).\n  - \\&#96;useSessionNotes\\&#96;: Allows saving AI chat messages as session notes.\n\n- **Actions**\n  - \\&#96;initiateDatabaseTableQuery\\&#96;: Triggers a search/query against a database table.\n  - \\&#96;xataToXYFlow\\&#96;: Converts database/AI results into graph nodes/edges for visualization.\n  - \\&#96;askAIAction\\&#96;: Sends a question to the AI for a specific table/model.\n\n- **AI Integration**\n  - \\&#96;useAssistant\\&#96; (from \\&#96;@ai-sdk/react\\&#96;): Manages AI chat state, message history, input, and error handling.\n\n- **UI Components**\n  - \\&#96;OracleInput\\&#96;: Input field with command/model context.\n  - \\&#96;OracleCommandMenu\\&#96;: Command palette for selecting actions (chat, search, scrape, etc.).\n  - \\&#96;UltraterrestrialModelSelection\\&#96;: Model/entity type selector.\n  - \\&#96;MindMapMessages\\&#96;: Renders chat/AI messages.\n  - \\&#96;SessionNotes\\&#96;: Displays session notes.\n\n---\n\n## Features and Behaviors\n\n### 1. **Session and Message Persistence**\n- Generates or retrieves a unique session ID (UUID) per user/session, stored in \\&#96;localStorage\\&#96;.\n- Persists chat messages to \\&#96;localStorage\\&#96;",

      "codeBlock": {
        "contents": "The application integrates with various AI and data services including OpenAI, Anthropic, Mem0, and others. All interactions with these APIs should be carefully documented and tested. Error handling must be implemented to gracefully manage API failures. The &#96;.mdc&#96; files will serve as the central repository for API specifications and schemas.\n\n### Server Actions vs API Routes\n\n*   **Server Actions are the preferred method** for all AI interactions, data processing, and external API integrations.\n*   Server Actions provide better type safety, reduced client-server boundary complexity, and improved performance over traditional API routes.\n*   When implementing new features that require server communication:\n    *   ✅ DO: Create a Server Action in the relevant feature directory with the &#96;.server.ts&#96; suffix\n    *   ❌ DON'T: Create a new API route unless absolutely required for external access\n*   Only use API routes (&#96;apps/app/src/app/api&#96; directory) when:\n    *   External services need webhook endpoints\n    *   Public API access is required\n    *   Third-party integrations specifically require REST endpoints\n*   For streaming operations (like AI completions), use Server Actions with streaming responses.\n*   All Server Actions should implement proper error handling and validation.\n\nThe knowledge base should be properly indexed and referenced in AI features.\n\n### Xata Integration Rules\n\n*   **Immediate Priority**: Support for Non Postgres Wire Enabled Xata database instances is the top priority.\n*   The system should maintain support for both Postgres Wire enabled and Non Postgres Wire Enabled Xata database instances.\n* When encountering \"type mismatch\" errors with Xata, particularly \"type [string] is not valid for field [rules]\", the &#96;rules&#96; parameter in &#96;xataToXYFlow&#96; and &#96;initiateStreamingQuery&#96; can accept either a string or an array of strings. If a string is provided, it will be converted to an array internally.\n\n## UI DEVELOPMENT GUIDELINES\n\n",
        "detailedLines": [

          },

          },

          },

            "text": "*   Server Actions provide better type safety, reduced client-server boundary complexity, and improved performance over traditional API routes."

            "text": "    *   ✅ DO: Create a Server Action in the relevant feature directory with the &#96;.server.ts&#96; suffix"

            "text": "    *   ❌ DON'T: Create a new API route unless absolutely required for external access"

If a string is provided, it will be converted to an array internally."
          },

            "text": "## UI DEVELOPMENT GUIDELINES"

          },

            "text": "UI development should adhere to the established component patterns in the &#96;components&#96; directory.         "contents": "- **Scalability Roadmap**\n    - Multi-database Support - Provider registry supports multiple databases\n    - Enhanced Search - More sophisticated search capabilities\n    - Performance Optimization - Continued query and type system optimization\n    - Advanced AI Integration - More sophisticated AI-powered features\n\n### Resources\n\n- [Xata Documentation](https://xata.io/docs)\n- [Bun Documentation](https://bun.sh/docs)\n- [TypeScript Handbook](https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/)\n\n### Internal Documentation\n\n- &#96;packages/db/IMPORT_GUIDE.md&#96; - Comprehensive usage guide\n- &#96;packages/db/QUICK_REFERENCE.md&#96; - Common patterns and examples\n- &#96;packages/db/TYPE_SYSTEM_SUMMARY.md&#96; - Type system overview\n- &#96;packages/db/xata/api/XataAskSDK_DOCUMENTATION.md&#96; - AI features documentation\n\n*Last Updated: 2025-06-25*\n*Package Versions: @db v0.1.0*\n\n## CODING STANDARDS\n\n* Code should be well-documented and follow consistent formatting.\n* All code must adhere to TypeScript type safety.\n* Use named exports for functions, avoiding default exports.\n* Error handling should be robust and informative. Custom error types should be used where appropriate.\n* Unit tests should aim for high coverage.\n* All callback functions should utilize &#96;useCallback&#96; to prevent unnecessary re-renders.\n* When using Next.js App Router, ensure that components using React hooks are marked with the &#96;\"use client\"&#96; directive to prevent errors in server components.\n* Split pages into server and client components as needed to accommodate hook usage.\n* Follow functional programming patterns rather than class-based implementations.\n* Use PascalCase for component files and lowercase with dashes for directories.\n\n## WORKFLOW \u0026 RELEASE RULES\n\n",

        "originalContents": "- **Scalability Roadmap**\n    - Multi-database Support - Provider registry supports multiple databases\n    - Enhanced Search - More sophisticated search capabilities\n    - Performance Optimization - Continued query and type system optimization\n    - Advanced AI Integration - More sophisticated AI-powered features\n\n### Resources\n\n- [Xata Documentation](https://xata.io/docs)\n- [Bun Documentation](https://bun.sh/docs)\n- [TypeScript Handbook](https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/)\n\n### Internal Documentation\n\n- &#96;packages/db/IMPORT_GUIDE.md&#96; - Comprehensive usage guide\n- &#96;packages/db/QUICK_REFERENCE.md&#96; - Common patterns and examples\n- &#96;packages/db/TYPE_SYSTEM_SUMMARY.md&#96; - Type system overview\n- &#96;packages/db/xata/api/XataAskSDK_DOCUMENTATION.md&#96; - AI features documentation\n\n*Last Updated: 2025-06-25*\n*Package Versions: @db v0.1.0*\n\n## CODING STANDARDS\n\n* Code should be well-documented and follow consistent formatting.\n* All code must adhere to TypeScript type safety.\n* Use named exports for functions, avoiding default exports.\n* Error handling should be robust and informative. Custom error types should be used where appropriate.\n* Unit tests should aim for high coverage.\n* All callback functions should utilize &#96;useCallback&#96; to prevent unnecessary re-renders.\n* When using Next.js App Router, ensure that components using React hooks are marked with the &#96;\"use client\"&#96; directive to prevent errors in server components.\n* Split pages into server and client components as needed to accommodate hook usage.\n* Follow functional programming patterns rather than class-based implementations.\n* Use PascalCase for component files and lowercase with dashes for directories.\n\n## WORKFLOW \u0026 RELEASE RULES\n\n",

      "codeBlock": {
        "contents": "# Technology Stack\n\n## Build System \u0026 Package Management\n- **Runtime**: Bun (JavaScript/TypeScript), Python 3.9+\n- **Monorepo**: Turborepo with workspace configuration\n- **Package Manager**: Bun for JS/TS, pip/conda for Python\n\n## Frontend Stack\n- **Framework**: Next.js 15.3.5 with App Router\n- **React**: 19.1.0 with React Server Components\n- **Styling**: Tailwind CSS 4.1.11 + Radix UI components\n- **3D Graphics**: Three.js, React Three Fiber, React Three Drei\n- **Animations**: Framer Motion, GSAP\n- **State Management**: Zustand, React Context\n- **Real-time**: Liveblocks, PartySocket\n\n## Backend \u0026 Data\n- **Database**: Xata (PostgreSQL) with vector search capabilities\n- **Vector Storage**: Multi-backend (Upstash Vector, FAISS, pgvector)\n- **AI/ML**: OpenAI, Anthropic, Groq via Vercel AI SDK\n- **Authentication**: Clerk\n- **File Storage**: Vercel Blob, Xata file attachments\n\n## Python RAG System\n- **Framework**: FastAPI, Streamlit\n- **AI/ML**: LangChain, sentence-transformers, torch\n- **Vector DBs**: FAISS, Upstash Vector, CocoIndex (pgvector)\n- **Document Processing**: PyPDF2, PyMuPDF, BeautifulSoup4\n- **CLI**: Charm CLI tools (gum, huh, glow, glamour)\n\n## Development Tools\n- **TypeScript**: 5.8+ with strict configuration\n- **Linting**: ESLint 9.30+ with Next.js config\n- **Component Development**: Storybook 8.6+\n- **Testing**: Jest, Storybook testing utilities\n- **Code Generation**: Plop for component scaffolding\n\n## Common Commands\n\n### Development\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n# Start main app\nbun run dev:app\n\n# Start Storybook\nbun run storybook\n\n# Python RAG system\ncd apps/disclosure-rag\npython streamlit_app.py    # Dashboard\npython api_server.py       # API server\npython cli.py             # Interactive CLI\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Build \u0026 Deploy\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n# Build main app\nbun run build:app\n\n# Start production\nbun run start:app\n\n# Component audit\nbun run audit:components\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Data Operations\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n# Export Xata data\nbun run export:xata\n\n# Import data\nbun run import:data\nbun run import:events\n",

        "contents": "---\ndescription: Guide for using Task Master to manage task-driven development workflows\nglobs: **/*\nalwaysApply: true\n---\n# Task Master Development Workflow\n\nThis guide outlines the typical process for using Task Master to manage software development projects.\n\n## Primary Interaction: MCP Server vs. CLI\n\nTask Master offers two primary ways to interact:\n\n1.  **MCP Server (Recommended for Integrated Tools)**:\n    - For AI agents and integrated development environments (like Cursor), interacting via the **MCP server is the preferred method**.\n    - The MCP server exposes Task Master functionality through a set of tools (e.g., &#96;get_tasks&#96;, &#96;add_subtask&#96;).\n    - This method offers better performance, structured data exchange, and richer error handling compared to CLI parsing.\n    - Refer to [&#96;mcp.mdc&#96;](mdc:.cursor/rules/mcp.mdc) for details on the MCP architecture and available tools.\n    - A comprehensive list and description of MCP tools and their corresponding CLI commands can be found in [&#96;taskmaster.mdc&#96;](mdc:.cursor/rules/taskmaster.mdc).\n    - **Restart the MCP server** if core logic in &#96;scripts/modules&#96; or MCP tool/direct function definitions change.\n\n2.  **&#96;task-master&#96; CLI (For Users \u0026 Fallback)**:\n    - The global &#96;task-master&#96; command provides a user-friendly interface for direct terminal interaction.\n    - It can also serve as a fallback if the MCP server is inaccessible or a specific function isn't exposed via MCP.\n    - Install globally with &#96;npm install -g task-master-ai&#96; or use locally via &#96;npx task-master-ai ...&#96;.\n    - The CLI commands often mirror the MCP tools (e.g., &#96;task-master list&#96; corresponds to &#96;get_tasks&#96;).\n    - Refer to [&#96;taskmaster.mdc&#96;](mdc:.cursor/rules/taskmaster.mdc) for a detailed command reference.\n\n## Standard Development Workflow Process\n\n",

        "originalContents": "---\ndescription: Guide for using Task Master to manage task-driven development workflows\nglobs: **/*\nalwaysApply: true\n---\n# Task Master Development Workflow\n\nThis guide outlines the typical process for using Task Master to manage software development projects.\n\n## Primary Interaction: MCP Server vs. CLI\n\nTask Master offers two primary ways to interact:\n\n1.  **MCP Server (Recommended for Integrated Tools)**:\n    - For AI agents and integrated development environments (like Cursor), interacting via the **MCP server is the preferred method**.\n    - The MCP server exposes Task Master functionality through a set of tools (e.g., &#96;get_tasks&#96;, &#96;add_subtask&#96;).\n    - This method offers better performance, structured data exchange, and richer error handling compared to CLI parsing.\n    - Refer to [&#96;mcp.mdc&#96;](mdc:.cursor/rules/mcp.mdc) for details on the MCP architecture and available tools.\n    - A comprehensive list and description of MCP tools and their corresponding CLI commands can be found in [&#96;taskmaster.mdc&#96;](mdc:.cursor/rules/taskmaster.mdc).\n    - **Restart the MCP server** if core logic in &#96;scripts/modules&#96; or MCP tool/direct function definitions change.\n\n2.  **&#96;task-master&#96; CLI (For Users \u0026 Fallback)**:\n    - The global &#96;task-master&#96; command provides a user-friendly interface for direct terminal interaction.\n    - It can also serve as a fallback if the MCP server is inaccessible or a specific function isn't exposed via MCP.\n    - Install globally with &#96;npm install -g task-master-ai&#96; or use locally via &#96;npx task-master-ai ...&#96;.\n    - The CLI commands often mirror the MCP tools (e.g., &#96;task-master list&#96; corresponds to &#96;get_tasks&#96;).\n    - Refer to [&#96;taskmaster.mdc&#96;](mdc:.cursor/rules/taskmaster.mdc) for a detailed command reference.\n\n## Standard Development Workflow Process\n\n",

        "contents": "TipTap-based research editor with AI integration.\n\n## Shared Packages (&#96;/packages/&#96;)\n\n### Database (&#96;/packages/db/&#96;)\nXata integration with 29 entity models and 230,998+ records.\n\n**Key Files:**\n- &#96;xata/models/&#96; - Database entity definitions\n- &#96;xata/api/&#96; - Database utilities (ask, search, xyflow integration)\n- &#96;xata/client.ts&#96; - Xata client configuration\n\n### AI (&#96;/packages/ai/&#96;)\nAI processing components and external service integrations.\n\n**Key Areas:**\n- &#96;components/&#96; - AI UI components\n- &#96;integrations/&#96; - External APIs (EXA, Firecrawl, Tavily)\n- &#96;prometheus/&#96; - Advanced AI system\n\n### Services (&#96;/packages/services/&#96;)\nExternal service clients and deep research capabilities.\n\n### Knowledge Base (&#96;/packages/knowledge-base/&#96;)\nDocument management with 448+ documents across case files and transcripts.\n\n## File Naming Conventions\n\n### Components\n- **PascalCase** for React components: &#96;EntityNetworkGraph.tsx&#96;\n- **kebab-case** for files: &#96;entity-network-graph.tsx&#96;\n- **Storybook stories**: &#96;ComponentName.stories.tsx&#96;\n\n### Features\n- **kebab-case** directories: &#96;mindmap/&#96;, &#96;data-viz/&#96;\n- **camelCase** for hooks: &#96;useSpatialGrouping.ts&#96;\n- **PascalCase** for contexts: &#96;MindmapContext.tsx&#96;\n\n### Database\n- **kebab-case** for model files: &#96;event-subject-matter-experts.ts&#96;\n- **camelCase** for API utilities: &#96;askXata.ts&#96;\n\n## Import Patterns\n\n### Workspace Imports\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\nimport { XataClient } from '@db/xata'\nimport { askXata } from '@db/xata/api'\nimport { AIComponent } from '@repo/ai'\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Relative Imports\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// Within same feature\nimport { MindmapNode } from './components'\nimport { useSpatialGrouping } from '../hooks'\n\n// Cross-feature (avoid when possible)\nimport { DataVizComponent } from '../../data-viz'\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Code Organization Principles\n\n### Feature-First Structure\nGroup related functionality together rather than by file type:\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nfeatures/mindmap/\n├── components/\n├── hooks/\n├── utils/\n├── types/\n└── index.ts\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n",

        "contents": "\n## TECH STACK\n\nThis project utilizes Next.js, React, and TypeScript for frontend development. The backend utilizes a combination of serverless functions and AI services. Specific libraries include Three.js, react-three-fiber, GSAP for animations, Tailwind CSS for styling, shadcn UI components, and various AI integration libraries (OpenAI, Anthropic, Mem0). The project also utilizes knowledge base tools for data retrieval and processing, as well as 3D visualization libraries for UFO and space-related visualizations.  Python libraries used in the &#96;disclosure-rag&#96; package include: &#96;zstandard&#96;, &#96;zipp&#96;, &#96;yt_dlp&#96;, &#96;youtube_transcript_api&#96;, &#96;yarl&#96;, &#96;yaml&#96;, &#96;wrapt&#96;, &#96;websockets&#96;, &#96;websocket_client&#96;, &#96;wcwidth&#96;, &#96;wcmatch&#96;, &#96;watchfiles&#96;, &#96;uvloop&#96;, &#96;uvicorn&#96;, &#96;uv&#96;, &#96;urllib3&#96;, &#96;uncertainties&#96;, &#96;tzdata&#96;, &#96;typing_inspect&#96;, &#96;typing_extensions&#96;, &#96;types_requests&#96;, &#96;typer&#96;, &#96;traitlets&#96;, &#96;tqdm&#96;, &#96;tornado&#96;, &#96;tomli_w&#96;, &#96;tomli&#96;, &#96;toml&#96;, &#96;tokenizers&#96;, &#96;tiktoken_ext&#96;, &#96;tiktoken&#96;, &#96;tenacity&#96;, &#96;tabulate&#96;, &#96;sympy&#96;, &#96;streamlit_react_flow&#96;, &#96;streamlit_molstar&#96;, &#96;streamlit_file_browser&#96;, &#96;streamlit_embeded&#96;, &#96;streamlit_antd&#96;, &#96;streamlit_ace&#96;, &#96;streamlit&#96;, &#96;starlette&#96;, &#96;stack_data&#96;, &#96;sqlalchemy&#96;, &#96;spglib&#96;, &#96;soupsieve&#96;, &#96;sniffio&#96;, &#96;smmap&#96;, &#96;six&#96;, &#96;shellingham&#96;, &#96;sentry_sdk&#96;.\n\nA &#96;TECH_STACK.md&#96; document exists in the project root. It outlines the major technologies, frameworks, and tools used across the Ultraterrestrial Resurrection monorepo packages, including:\n\n### Package Structure\n\n- &#96;@/app&#96; - Main application\n- &#96;@/disclosure-rag&#96; - RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) system\n- &#96;@/db&#96; - Database layer and models\n\n### Database \u0026 Data Layer (&#96;@/db&#96;)\n\n- **Primary Database**: [Xata](https://xata.io/) - Serverless database platform\n    - PostgreSQL-based with additional features\n    - Built-in AI/Ask SDK for natural language queries\n    - Vector embeddings support (1536 dimensions)\n    - Branch-based development workflow\n    - Automatic API generation and type safety\n",
        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "lineNumber": 13
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 14,
            "text": "### Ticket Tracking"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 15
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 16,
            "text": "Tickets will be managed using Markdown files in the &#96;tickets&#96; directory. Each ticket will follow a consistent template outlining its goal, acceptance criteria, implementation notes, out-of-scope items, and test strategy. The status of each ticket will be indicated using the following keys: ✅ done, ⏳ pending, 🛑 blocked. The &#96;tickets/README.md&#96; file will contain an overview of the ticket system and naming conventions. The AI assistant should review &#96;README.md&#96; before starting work on a ticket. New utility functions should have accompanying test files created in a &#96;__tests__&#96; subdirectory within the relevant module directory.  A new &#96;DisclosureRagRecovered_Migration.md&#96; file will document the migration of code from &#96;disclosure-rag-recovered&#96; to &#96;disclosure-rag&#96;.  This will include a detailed specification of each ticket, including title, description, acceptance criteria, implementation notes, references, effort estimation, and testing guidelines.  All tickets related to the migration of the &#96;disclosure-rag-recovered&#96; package should be created in the &#96;tickets&#96; directory, following the guidelines specified in &#96;ticket-workflow.mdc&#96;.  The following files were identified for migration from &#96;disclosure-rag-recovered&#96; to &#96;disclosure-rag&#96;: &#96;disclosure_chat.py&#96;, &#96;agno_disclosure_chat.py&#96;, &#96;agno_disclosure_chat_with_files.py&#96;, &#96;main.sh&#96;, &#96;README_AGNO_CHAT.md&#96;, &#96;README_DISCLOSURE_CHAT.md&#96;, and &#96;research/ner_summary_to_xata_table_prompt.py.bak&#96;.  These migration tasks should be documented as separate tickets within the &#96;tickets&#96; directory, following the template specified in &#96;ticket-workflow.mdc&#96;.  All migration planning, specifications, and pseudocode should be tracked in the &#96;tickets/&#96; directory.  All migration tickets should be created in the &#96;tickets/&#96; directory and follow the &#96;ticket-workflow.mdc&#96; guidelines.  All tickets related to the migration should be created in the &#96;tickets&#96; directory.  The &#96;.md&#96; files detailing the pseudocode and migration specification should also be added to the tickets directory. All migration tickets should be created in the &#96;tickets/&#96; directory and follow the &#96;ticket-workflow.mdc&#96; guidelines."

Specific libraries include Three.js, react-three-fiber, GSAP for animations, Tailwind CSS for styling, shadcn UI components, and various AI integration libraries (OpenAI, Anthropic, Mem0). The project also utilizes knowledge base tools for data retrieval and processing, as well as 3D visualization libraries for UFO and space-related visualizations.  Python libraries used in the &#96;disclosure-rag&#96; package include: &#96;zstandard&#96;, &#96;zipp&#96;, &#96;yt_dlp&#96;, &#96;youtube_transcript_api&#96;, &#96;yarl&#96;, &#96;yaml&#96;, &#96;wrapt&#96;, &#96;websockets&#96;, &#96;websocket_client&#96;, &#96;wcwidth&#96;, &#96;wcmatch&#96;, &#96;watchfiles&#96;, &#96;uvloop&#96;, &#96;uvicorn&#96;, &#96;uv&#96;, &#96;urllib3&#96;, &#96;uncertainties&#96;, &#96;tzdata&#96;, &#96;typing_inspect&#96;, &#96;typing_extensions&#96;, &#96;types_requests&#96;, &#96;typer&#96;, &#96;traitlets&#96;, &#96;tqdm&#96;, &#96;tornado&#96;, &#96;tomli_w&#96;, &#96;tomli&#96;, &#96;toml&#96;, &#96;tokenizers&#96;, &#96;tiktoken_ext&#96;, &#96;tiktoken&#96;, &#96;tenacity&#96;, &#96;tabulate&#96;, &#96;sympy&#96;, &#96;streamlit_react_flow&#96;, &#96;streamlit_molstar&#96;, &#96;streamlit_file_browser&#96;, &#96;streamlit_embeded&#96;, &#96;streamlit_antd&#96;, &#96;streamlit_ace&#96;, &#96;streamlit&#96;, &#96;starlette&#96;, &#96;stack_data&#96;, &#96;sqlalchemy&#96;, &#96;spglib&#96;, &#96;soupsieve&#96;, &#96;sniffio&#96;, &#96;smmap&#96;, &#96;six&#96;, &#96;shellingham&#96;, &#96;sentry_sdk&#96;.\n\nA &#96;TECH_STACK.md&#96; document exists in the project root. It outlines the major technologies, frameworks, and tools used across the Ultraterrestrial Resurrection monorepo packages, including:\n\n### Package Structure\n\n- &#96;@/app&#96; - Main application\n- &#96;@/disclosure-rag&#96; - RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) system\n- &#96;@/db&#96; - Database layer and models\n\n### Database \u0026 Data Layer (&#96;@/db&#96;)\n\n- **Primary Database**: [Xata](https://xata.io/) - Serverless database platform\n    - PostgreSQL-based with additional features\n    - Built-in AI/Ask SDK for natural language queries\n    - Vector embeddings support (1536 dimensions)\n    - Branch-based development workflow\n    - Automatic API generation and type safety\n",

            "text": "Tickets will be managed using Markdown files in the &#96;tickets&#96; directory. The status of each ticket will be indicated using the following keys: ✅ done, ⏳ pending, 🛑 blocked. The &#96;tickets/README.md&#96; file will contain an overview of the ticket system and naming conventions. The AI assistant should review &#96;README.md&#96; before starting work on a ticket. Run a text search against the database to find the records that are most relevant to the question asked by the user.\n2. Take the most relevant results, and create a custom prompt for OpenAI.\n3. Send the prompt to the ChatGPT API and let the model complete the answer.\n\nThe &#96;ask&#96; endpoint can use either keyword or vector search to find records that are most relevant to the user's query. To learn more about keyword or vector searches, see our [blog the compares the two approaches](https://lite.xata.io/blog/keyword-vs-semantic-search-chatgpt).\n\nWhen you use the &#96;ask&#96; endpoint, you can choose to continue any conversation you've started. Xata will remember the rules and context you've set, and allow you to continue to ask follow-up questions.         "contents": "---\ndescription: Comprehensive reference for Taskmaster MCP tools and CLI commands.\nglobs: **/*\nalwaysApply: true\n---\n# Taskmaster Tool \u0026 Command Reference\n\nThis document provides a detailed reference for interacting with Taskmaster, covering both the recommended MCP tools, suitable for integrations like Cursor, and the corresponding &#96;task-master&#96; CLI commands, designed for direct user interaction or fallback.\n\n**Note:** For interacting with Taskmaster programmatically or via integrated tools, using the **MCP tools is strongly recommended** due to better performance, structured data, and error handling. The CLI commands serve as a user-friendly alternative and fallback. \n\n**Important:** Several MCP tools involve AI processing... The AI-powered tools include &#96;parse_prd&#96;, &#96;analyze_project_complexity&#96;, &#96;update_subtask&#96;, &#96;update_task&#96;, &#96;update&#96;, &#96;expand_all&#96;, &#96;expand_task&#96;, and &#96;add_task&#96;.\n\n---\n\n## Initialization \u0026 Setup\n\n### 1. Initialize Project (&#96;init&#96;)\n\n*   **MCP Tool:** &#96;initialize_project&#96;\n*   **CLI Command:** &#96;task-master init [options]&#96;\n*   **Description:** &#96;Set up the basic Taskmaster file structure and configuration in the current directory for a new project.&#96;\n*   **Key CLI Options:**\n    *   &#96;--name \u003cname\u003e&#96;: &#96;Set the name for your project in Taskmaster's configuration.&#96;\n    *   &#96;--description \u003ctext\u003e&#96;: &#96;Provide a brief description for your project.&#96;\n    *   &#96;--version \u003cversion\u003e&#96;: &#96;Set the initial version for your project, e.g., '0.1.0'.&#96;\n    *   &#96;-y, --yes&#96;: &#96;Initialize Taskmaster quickly using default settings without interactive prompts.&#96;\n*   **Usage:** Run this once at the beginning of a new project.\n*   **MCP Variant Description:** &#96;Set up the basic Taskmaster file structure and configuration in the current directory for a new project by running the 'task-master init' command.&#96;\n",

        "contents": "# Project Structure\n\n## Monorepo Organization\nUltraTerrestrial follows a monorepo pattern with Turborepo, organized into applications and shared packages.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nultraterrestrial-resurrection/\n├── apps/                    # Applications (3 main apps)\n├── packages/               # Shared packages (5 packages)\n├── docs/                   # Project documentation\n├── scripts/                # Build and utility scripts\n└── *.md                   # Root documentation files\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Applications (&#96;/apps/&#96;)\n\n### Main App (&#96;/apps/app/&#96;)\nPrimary Next.js application with the research platform interface.\n\n**Key Structure:**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nsrc/\n├── app/                    # Next.js App Router\n│   ├── (auth)/            # Authentication routes\n│   ├── (site)/            # Public site routes\n│   └── api/               # API endpoints\n├── components/            # UI components (50+ categories)\n├── features/              # Feature modules\n│   ├── mindmap/           # Enhanced nodes, spatial grouping, tours\n│   ├── 3d/                # Three.js visualizations\n│   ├── ai/                # AI integration and chat\n│   └── data-viz/          # Data visualization components\n├── hooks/                 # Custom React hooks\n├── lib/                   # Utility libraries\n└── utils/                 # Helper functions\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Disclosure RAG (&#96;/apps/disclosure-rag/&#96;)\nPython-based RAG system with triple backend architecture.\n\n**Key Structure:**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nlib/\n├── adapters/              # RAG system adapters\n├── storage/               # Vector storage backends\n├── entity_extraction/     # NER and entity processing\n└── visualization/         # Data visualization tools\nagents/                    # AI agent implementations\nscripts/                   # Batch processing scripts\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Research Canvas (&#96;/apps/research-canvas/&#96;)\n",

        "contents": "*   **Usage:** Run this after making changes to tasks.json to keep individual task files up to date.\n\n---\n\n## Environment Variables Configuration (Updated)\n\nTaskmaster primarily uses the **&#96;.taskmaster/config.json&#96;** file (in project root) for configuration (models, parameters, logging level, etc.), managed via &#96;task-master models --setup&#96;.\n\nEnvironment variables are used **only** for sensitive API keys related to AI providers and specific overrides like the Ollama base URL:\n\n*   **API Keys (Required for corresponding provider):**\n    *   &#96;ANTHROPIC_API_KEY&#96;\n    *   &#96;PERPLEXITY_API_KEY&#96;\n    *   &#96;OPENAI_API_KEY&#96;\n    *   &#96;GOOGLE_API_KEY&#96;\n    *   &#96;MISTRAL_API_KEY&#96;\n    *   &#96;AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY&#96; (Requires &#96;AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT&#96; too)\n    *   &#96;OPENROUTER_API_KEY&#96;\n    *   &#96;XAI_API_KEY&#96;\n    *   &#96;OLLANA_API_KEY&#96; (Requires &#96;OLLAMA_BASE_URL&#96; too)\n*   **Endpoints (Optional/Provider Specific inside .taskmaster/config.json):**\n    *   &#96;AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT&#96;\n    *   &#96;OLLAMA_BASE_URL&#96; (Default: &#96;http://localhost:11434/api&#96;)\n\n**Set API keys** in your **&#96;.env&#96;** file in the project root (for CLI use) or within the &#96;env&#96; section of your **&#96;.cursor/mcp.json&#96;** file (for MCP/Cursor integration). All other settings (model choice, max tokens, temperature, log level, custom endpoints) are managed in &#96;.taskmaster/config.json&#96; via &#96;task-master models&#96; command or &#96;models&#96; MCP tool.\n\n---\n\nFor details on how these commands fit into the development process, see the [Development Workflow Guide](mdc:.cursor/rules/dev_workflow.mdc).\n",

@@ -1,1 +1,122 @@
- 
+ # AI SDK 5 Beta Usage Guidelines
+ 
+ ## Introduction
+ 
+ This rule provides guidelines for implementing and migrating to Vercel AI SDK 5 beta in our project. AI SDK 5 introduces a redesigned architecture with LanguageModelV2, new message types (UIMessage and ModelMessage), SSE streaming, and agentic controls. These changes improve type safety, extensibility, and control over AI interactions.
+ 
+ Follow these patterns to ensure consistent AI integration across components and hooks. Reference existing usage in [useBackendChat](mdc:apps/app/src/hooks/useBackendChat.ts) and [ChatSidebar](mdc:apps/app/src/components/chat-sidebar.tsx) when updating.
+ 
+ ## Key Changes from AI SDK 4
+ 
+ - New LanguageModelV2 protocol treating all outputs as content parts
+ - Separate UIMessage (for UI) and ModelMessage (for model input)
+ - Transport-based useChat configuration
+ - Server-Sent Events (SSE) for streaming
+ - Agentic features: prepareStep and stopWhen
+ - Type-safe tool calls and metadata
+ 
+ For detailed migration, see the [official migration guide](https://v5.ai-sdk.dev/docs/migration).
+ 
+ ## Implementation Patterns
+ 
+ ### Basic Chat Setup
+ 
+ Use the new transport system for chat hooks:
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;typescript
+ // ✅ DO: Use DefaultChatTransport for configuration
+ import { useChat } from '@ai-sdk/react';
+ import { DefaultChatTransport } from 'ai';
+ 
+ const { messages, sendMessage } = useChat({
+   transport: new DefaultChatTransport({
+     api: '/api/chat',
+     headers: { 'Custom-Header': 'value' },
+   }),
+ });
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;typescript
+ // ❌ DON'T: Use old useChat without transport
+ const { messages } = useChat({ api: '/api/chat' });
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ### Message Handling
+ 
+ Always convert UIMessages to ModelMessages before sending to models:
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;typescript
+ // ✅ DO: Explicit conversion with metadata
+ import { convertToModelMessages, streamText } from 'ai';
+ 
+ const result = await streamText({
+   model: openai('gpt-4o'),
+   messages: convertToModelMessages(uiMessages),
+ });
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ Add type-safe metadata:
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;typescript
+ // Define schema
+ const metadataSchema = z.object({
+   duration: z.number().optional(),
+   model: z.string().optional(),
+ });
+ 
+ // Add to stream
+ result.toUIMessageStreamResponse({
+   metadata: { duration: 1500, model: 'gpt-4o' } as z.infer&lt;typeof metadataSchema&gt;,
+ });
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ### Tool Usage
+ 
+ Define tools with input/output schemas for type safety:
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;typescript
+ // ✅ DO: Type-safe tools
+ import { tool } from 'ai';
+ import { z } from 'zod';
+ 
+ const weatherTool = tool({
+   description: 'Get weather information',
+   inputSchema: z.object({ city: z.string() }),
+   outputSchema: z.object({
+     temperature: z.number(),
+     conditions: z.string(),
+   }),
+   execute: async ({ city }) =&gt; ({
+     temperature: 72,
+     conditions: 'sunny',
+   }),
+ });
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ## Migration Steps
+ 
+ 1. Update package: &#96;bun add ai@beta @ai-sdk/openai@beta @ai-sdk/react@beta&#96;
+ 2. Replace useChat with transport configuration
+ 3. Implement UIMessage/ModelMessage conversion
+ 4. Update streaming to SSE
+ 5. Add type-safe tools and metadata where appropriate
+ 
+ Test thoroughly, especially streaming and tool calls.
+ 
+ ## Common Pitfalls
+ 
+ - Forgetting to convert UIMessages to ModelMessages before model calls
+ - Not handling new content part types in UI rendering
+ - Missing 'use client' in components using hooks
+ - Overlooking transport configuration for custom headers
+ 
+ ## Resources
+ 
+ - [AI SDK 5 Beta Announcement](https://v5.ai-sdk.dev/docs/announcing-ai-sdk-5-beta)
+ - [Official Docs](https://v5.ai-sdk.dev/docs)
+ description:
+ globs:
+ alwaysApply: false
+ 
+ ---
+
